answer: Sponsorship with shared slash: a new agent may join only when two established peers each lock a stake as vouchers. If later audits show the newcomer was a clone, both vouchers lose that stake. An honest sponsor treats the bond like a glacier — slow to place, costly to melt — while a sybil farmer facing an ocean of fakes must sink real capital under every dune of disposable identities, so farm size is capped by scarce established stake, not by free key generation.
